intent: independent new narrative scenes, dated clothing reference and handbook/place plates

jobs.scene: Front, left-side and back views of the same protagonist with his newly fitted overlapping skin wrap, plain crown pad and original bast soles.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: dated clothing reference sheet for Humanity Handbook, Moon 3 Day 5, continuous Day 63.
Create ONE coherent landscape character reference sheet on warm ivory paper, fine brown ink and watercolour. Match the original man's lean adult identity, dark wavy ear-length hair, short beard, nose/brow and natural smooth skin from Image 1. Image 1 is IDENTITY/STYLE only, not clothing state. Image 2 supplies ONLY the existing cap, footbeds and underlying waist garments; replace its grass torso outfit by the newly made skin wrap described below. Retain realistic ordinary anatomy, not a fantasy hero.

Layout: three full-length views, FRONT, LEFT SIDE and BACK, plus one small closure detail. All views show the same one-piece garment and existing footwear. Readable restrained title exactly "HUMANITY HANDBOOK", smaller subtitle exactly "Character reference — Moon 3 Day 5". Labels "FRONT", "LEFT SIDE", "BACK", "CHEST TIE". No other text necessary.

NEW main garment: ONE previously worked, worn deer-sized skin fitted as an overlapping shoulder/body WRAP. The brown short animal hair is INWARD against the body. The outward surface is dull warm TAN skin, softly irregular and worn, not a thick furry orange cape. It covers BOTH shoulders, back, chest and abdomen, with two front margins OVERLAPPING; an irregular hem ends just ABOVE THE KNEES. Upper edge turned slightly shows a narrow line of brown inner hair. No sleeves: arms emerge naturally at the side openings; no modern armholes or tailored jacket. A small repaired folded area is on anatomical LEFT shoulder (front viewer RIGHT). One short cord closes the overlap BELOW THE THROAT across upper chest, readily released, no tight neck loop or decorative buckle. The existing narrow waist fastening lightly gathers the wrap over the hips, without a wide manufactured belt.
Beneath the closed wrap are old bark waist layers and small pale rabbit pelvic pad, mostly CONCEALED. The separate narrow rust fox strip is RETAINED under the anatomical LEFT shoulder, normally concealed; do not make a broad fox-fur collar. BOTH old grass torso screens are STORED elsewhere and NOT WORN: no dangling grass fringe below this wrap and no extra mats on this sheet.

Still visible: the same LOW plain grey-brown rabbit-fur crown pad with folded margin and loose forehead/back band; human face and ears and much nape exposed, no rabbit head, muzzle, eyes, upright ears or tail. Both feet wear the same thin flat woven willow-bast soles, corded margins and low ties with open toes and exposed ankles. Both lower legs are bare. No new hood, trousers, leggings, leather shoes or second animal skin.
Show natural hands and exactly two legs per view. Skin is smoothly washed without etched scars, tattoos, patterns or excessive hatching. Keep the tan wrap readable in front/back/side rather than an inventory display. All reference images are limited-role inputs; do not reproduce Image 1's shelter or Image 2's old grass clothing.

jobs.page: 01_Survival/Moon 3 Day 2 - Let the Rock Carry the Roof.md
jobs.scene: Inspecting the dry central strip of the newly discovered overhang, before construction or the move.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE wide 16:9 narrative illustration for Humanity Handbook, in fine brown ink and luminous restrained watercolour with soft warm-paper edges, matching Image 1.
Image 1 is the original man's IDENTITY/STYLE only, not its early clothing state or exact pose. Image 2 is the dated CLOTHING reference only, no sheet labels/layout in this picture. Keep the same lean adult about thirty, dark wavy ear-length hair and short beard, natural smoothly washed skin with no scars/tattoos or etched patterns.
One ordinary figure has exactly two legs and two natural hands. No labelled diagrams, text, watermark, magical future equipment, modern objects or invented possessions.
Full current clothing BEFORE Day 63: low plain grey-brown rabbit-fur crown pad with folded margins and loose forehead/back band, face/ears exposed, NO animal head/eyes/muzzle/ears/tail. ONE narrow rust fox strip on anatomical LEFT shoulder (front viewer RIGHT), TWO separate hanging grass screens front/back with light retaining rows, open flanks, bark waist layers and pale pelvic pad beneath, and BOTH thin flat woven bast soles with low ties, open toes and exposed ankles. The grass is soft hanging bundles, not mat armour. Show the back screen edge naturally where the angle permits. No new skin wrap is worn.
Site: shallow southeast-facing pale limestone overhang above the familiar northern Iberian valley, late autumn with sparse ochre leaves and cool slate distance. It is a projecting low ledge over a modest shallow recess, not a deep cavern, carved masonry wall, log cabin or tall cliff cathedral. One damp fissured corner is outside the occupied strip. The dry central rock roof takes most of the cover; no timber roof is built beneath it.
Scene Moon 3 Day 2 / Day 60: the traveller stands naturally near the edge of the open recess, almost frontal, looking at the drip line and dry leaves on the floor. Full body and both bast soles readable; LEFT fox strip viewer RIGHT. His hands rest, no touching or levering overhead rock. A plain integral wooden spear rests on accessible ground nearby if needed; avoid additional equipment.
The place is UNBUILT and UNINHABITED at this moment: NO screen, bed, rack, hearth, pots, stacks of supplies, new skin garment or other person. Compose man centre-right, low projecting roof upper-left and valley breathing space to the right. Quiet inspection, daylight, no visible moon.

attempts.reason: Unmade stone-hafted spear in discovery scene.
